newsitem.title: USA: Body of singer Jeff Buckley recovered in Memphis.
newsitem.headline: Body of singer Jeff Buckley recovered in Memphis.

text.p: The body of folk-rock singer Jeff Buckley has been recovered from the Mississippi River, police said on Thursday.

"There were no signs of foul play but the body was pretty swollen and had signs of decomposition," Memphis Police Lt. Richard True said. "He was found in the water not far from where he was last seen" swimming in a boat marina on May 29, True said.

A friend onshore told police Buckley had been in a good mood and decided to go for a swim fully clothed. Wake from a passing boat caused the friend to turn away to keep a portable stereo from being splashed and he lost sight of Buckley.
True said a passenger on a riverboat saw a body floating in the Mississippi River near downtown Memphis on Wednesday evening. The body turned out to be Buckley's.
The Shelby County coroner's office would not comment on a pending autopsy on Buckley, who was 30.
The latest Billboard magazine, published before Buckley's disappearance, said he was in Memphis last week to record an album that was scheduled to be released in early 1998.
Buckley emerged from the shadow of his late musician father Tim Buckley when he released his full-length debut album "Grace" on Columbia Records in 1994.

Critics heaped praise on him, with Entertainment Weekly magazine likening his haunting voice to a cross between Art Garfunkel and the late Freddie Mercury, the lead vocalist for Queen. David Bowie called "Grace" one of his recent favourites.

Buckley was born in November 1966, the only child from a brief marriage between then-unknown singer Tim Buckley and his wife, Mary. Father and son met only once, spending a week together just two months before Tim died of a heroin and morphine overdose in June 1975 at the age of 28.

Tim Buckley had been a highly respected singer/songwriter through the late 1960s who applied his versatile vocal and poetic gifts to a range of folk, jazz and blues-laced albums. Die-hard fans of the cult singer were quick to draw comparisons between the musical styles of the two Buckleys, but Jeff maintained an ambivalent attitude and was not afraid to mock his father's oddball notoriety.

Raised in southern California by his mother, and usually on the move, Buckley decided to become a musician when he was 12. He said in a Rolling Stone interview that the first album he owned was Led Zeppelin's "Physical Graffiti."
